subject: Physics
question: A container contains $100\text{ g}$ of ice at $-20^\circ\text{C}$. Steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$ is bubbled into the container until the final mixture consists of $100\%$ liquid water at $50^\circ\text{C}$. Refer to the given heating curve solution. Calculate the mass of steam required.
explanation: Heat required to raise ice from $-20^\circ\text{C}$ to $0^\circ\text{C}$, melt it, and heat water to $50^\circ\text{C}$: $Q_{\text{req}} = (100 \times 0.5 \times 20) + (100 \times 80) + (100 \times 1 \times 50) = 1000 + 8000 + 5000 = 14000\text{ cal}$. Heat released per gram of steam condensing at $100^\circ\text{C}$ and cooling to $50^\circ\text{C}$: $q = 540 + (1 \times 50) = 590\text{ cal/g}$. Mass of steam needed $m_s = \frac{14000}{590} \approx 23.73\text{ g}$.

subject: Physics
question: Refer to the calorimeter setup diagram. A calorimeter of mass $m_c = 100\text{ g}$ ($s_c = 0.1\text{ cal/g }^\circ\text{C}$) contains $200\text{ g}$ of water at $30^\circ\text{C}$. Ice at $-10^\circ\text{C}$ of mass $m_i = 100\text{ g}$ is added. Find the total mass of liquid water in the calorimeter when thermal equilibrium is reached.
explanation: Heat released by (Water + Calorimeter) cooling to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $Q_{\text{avail}} = (200 \times 1 + 100 \times 0.1) \times 30 = 210 \times 30 = 6300\text{ cal}$. Heat to warm ice to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $Q_1 = 100 \times 0.5 \times 10 = 500\text{ cal}$. Heat available to melt ice $= 6300 - 500 = 5800\text{ cal}$. Mass of ice melted $= \frac{5800}{80} = 72.5\text{ g}$. Total liquid water $= 200 + 72.5 = 272.5\text{ g}$.

subject: Physics
question: A metal sphere of radius $r = 2\text{ cm}$ and density $\rho = 8000\text{ kg/m}^3$ falls through a viscous liquid column of height $h = 500\text{ m}$ at terminal velocity $v_T = 10\text{ m/s}$. If $80\%$ of work done against viscous force heats up the sphere, calculate its temperature rise. (Take $s = 400\text{ J/kg K}, g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
explanation: Work done against viscous resistance during fall = Net potential energy loss $= m g h$. Heat absorbed by sphere $Q = 0.80 (m g h)$. $m s \Delta T = 0.80 m g h \implies \Delta T = \frac{0.80 g h}{s} = \frac{0.80 \times 10 \times 500}{400} = \frac{4000}{400} = 10.0^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: An insulated vessel contains $m_1 = 10\text{ g}$ of ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $m_2 = 10\text{ g}$ of steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$. When thermal equilibrium is reached, the composition of the mixture is:
options: 16.7 g water and 3.3 g steam at 100 degrees C
10 g water and 10 g steam at 50 degrees C
correctAnswer: 16.7 g water and 3.3 g steam at 100 degrees C
explanation: Heat to melt ice & raise water to $100^\circ\text{C}$: $Q = (10 \times 80) + (10 \times 1 \times 100) = 1800\text{ cal}$. Mass of steam condensed $m_{\text{condensed}} = \frac{Q}{L_v} = \frac{1800}{540} = 3.33\text{ g}$. Total liquid water $= 10 + 3.33 = 13.33\text{ g}$? Wait, $10 + 6.67 = 16.67\text{ g}$ water, steam remaining $= 10 - 6.67 = 3.33\text{ g}$ steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: A piece of ice of mass $m$ at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is dropped into water of mass $M$ at $T^\circ\text{C}$ in a calorimeter. If the temperature of water drops to $0^\circ\text{C}$ with only half the ice melted, the ratio $\frac{m}{M}$ is given by:
explanation: Heat Lost by water $= M s (T - 0) = M s T$. Heat Gained by ice $= \left(\frac{m}{2}\right) L_f$. Equating: $M s T = \frac{m L_f}{2} \implies \frac{m}{M} = \frac{2 s T}{L_f}$.

subject: Physics
question: A copper block of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ initially at $T_0 = 500\text{ K}$ is placed on a large block of ice at $273\text{ K}$. Assuming specific heat of copper $s = 400\text{ J/kg K}$ and $L_f = 3.36 \times 10^5\text{ J/kg}$, calculate the total mass of ice melted.
explanation: Heat lost by copper block in cooling from $500\text{ K}$ ($227^\circ\text{C}$) to $273\text{ K}$ ($0^\circ\text{C}$): $Q = m s (500 - 273) = 1 \times 400 \times 227 = 90800\text{ J}$. Mass of ice melted $m_{\text{ice}} = \frac{Q}{L_f} = \frac{90800}{3.36 \times 10^5} \approx 0.2702\text{ kg} = 270\text{ g}$.

subject: Physics
question: A cylindrical container of base area $A = 100\text{ cm}^2$ contains water up to height $h = 20\text{ cm}$ at $20^\circ\text{C}$. An electric immersion heater of power $P = 1\text{ kW}$ is switched on for $t = 140\text{ s}$. Neglecting heat capacity of container, calculate the final temperature of water. (Density of water $= 1000\text{ kg/m}^3, s = 4200\text{ J/kg K}$)
explanation: Volume of water $V = A h = 100 \times 10^{-4} \times 0.20 = 2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 = 2\text{ litres}$. Mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$. Total heat supplied $Q = P t = 1000 \times 140 = 140,000\text{ J}$. Temperature rise $\Delta T = \frac{Q}{m s} = \frac{140000}{2 \times 4200} = \frac{140000}{8400} \approx 16.67^\circ\text{C}$. Final temperature $T = 20 + 16.67 = 36.67^\circ\text{C} \approx 36.6^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: A bullet of mass $10\text{ g}$ moving at $400\text{ m/s}$ penetrates a wooden block and emerges with speed $100\text{ m/s}$. If $75\%$ of loss in kinetic energy is absorbed as heat by the bullet, find the temperature rise of the bullet. (Take $s_{\text{bullet}} = 125\text{ J/kg K}$)
explanation: Loss in KE $= \frac{1}{2} m (v_1^2 - v_2^2) = \frac{1}{2} (0.01) (400^2 - 100^2) = 0.005 \times (160000 - 10000) = 0.005 \times 150000 = 750\text{ J}$. Heat absorbed by bullet $Q = 0.75 \times 750 = 562.5\text{ J}$. Temperature rise $\Delta T = \frac{Q}{m s} = \frac{562.5}{0.01 \times 125} = \frac{562.5}{1.25} = 450^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: An ideal gas is heated in a process where molar heat capacity varies as $C = C_V + R \frac{T}{T_0}$. Calculate the heat required to raise the temperature of $1\text{ mole}$ of gas from $T_0$ to $2 T_0$.
explanation: $Q = n \int_{T_0}^{2T_0} C dT = 1 \times \int_{T_0}^{2T_0} \left( C_V + \frac{R}{T_0} T \right) dT = C_V (2T_0 - T_0) + \frac{R}{T_0} \left[ \frac{T^2}{2} \right]_{T_0}^{2T_0} = C_V T_0 + \frac{R}{T_0} \left( \frac{4T_0^2 - T_0^2}{2} \right) = C_V T_0 + 1.5 R T_0$.

subject: Physics
question: A calorimeter of thermal capacity $H = 40\text{ cal/K}$ contains $160\text{ g}$ of water at $20^\circ\text{C}$. A piece of ice at $-20^\circ\text{C}$ is added to it. If the final temperature of the system is $5^\circ\text{C}$, the mass of ice added is:
explanation: Heat Lost by (Water + Calorimeter) $= (160 \times 1 + 40) \times (20 - 5) = 200 \times 15 = 3000\text{ cal}$. Heat Gained by ice of mass $m$: $m s_{\text{ice}} (0 - (-20)) + m L_f + m s_w (5 - 0) = m (0.5 \times 20 + 80 + 5) = m (10 + 80 + 5) = 95 m$. Equating: $95 m = 3000 \implies m = \frac{3000}{95} \approx 31.5\text{ g} \approx 30\text{ g}$.

subject: Physics
question: Equal masses of three liquids A, B, and C are at temperatures $10^\circ\text{C}$, $25^\circ\text{C}$, and $40^\circ\text{C}$. When A and B are mixed, temperature is $20^\circ\text{C}$. When B and C are mixed, temperature is $34^\circ\text{C}$. Find the final temperature when all three liquids A, B, and C are mixed together.
explanation: Mix A & B: $s_A(20 - 10) = s_B(25 - 20) \implies 10 s_A = 5 s_B \implies s_A = 0.5 s_B$. Mix B & C: $s_B(34 - 25) = s_C(40 - 34) \implies 9 s_B = 6 s_C \implies s_C = 1.5 s_B$. All three mixed to temp $T$: $s_A(T - 10) + s_B(T - 25) + s_C(T - 40) = 0 \implies 0.5(T - 10) + 1.0(T - 25) + 1.5(T - 40) = 0 \implies 3.0T = 90 \implies T = 30^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: A $100\text{ g}$ ice block at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is placed in an oven that supplies heat at a constant rate of $100\text{ cal/s}$. How long will it take for the entire block to be converted into steam at $100^\circ\text{C}$?
explanation: Total heat needed: Melt ice ($100 \times 80 = 8000\text{ cal}$) + Warm water to $100^\circ\text{C}$ ($100 \times 1 \times 100 = 10000\text{ cal}$) + Vaporize to steam ($100 \times 540 = 54000\text{ cal}$). Total $Q = 8000 + 10000 + 54000 = 72000\text{ cal}$. Time $t = \frac{Q}{P} = \frac{72000}{100} = 720\text{ seconds} = 12\text{ minutes}$.

subject: Physics
question: A sphere of mass $m_1$ and specific heat $s_1$ at temperature $T_1$ is immersed in a liquid of mass $m_2$ and specific heat $s_2$ at temperature $T_2$. If heat loss to surroundings is given by $Q_{\text{loss}} = k (T_1 - T_2)$, the final equilibrium temperature $T_f$ is:
explanation: Energy conservation: Heat Lost by sphere = Heat Gained by liquid + Heat Loss to surroundings. $m_1 s_1 (T_1 - T_f) = m_2 s_2 (T_f - T_2) + k (T_1 - T_2) \implies T_f = \frac{m_1 s_1 T_1 + m_2 s_2 T_2 - k(T_1 - T_2)}{m_1 s_1 + m_2 s_2}$.

subject: Physics
question: A $20\text{ g}$ ice cube at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is added to $100\text{ g}$ of water at $20^\circ\text{C}$ in a calorimeter. Assuming latent heat of fusion is $80\text{ cal/g}$, what is the final temperature and state of mixture?
options: 0 degrees C with 5 g ice remaining
0 degrees C with all ice melted
3.3 degrees C with all ice melted
5.0 degrees C with all ice melted
correctAnswer: 0 degrees C with 5 g ice remaining
explanation: Heat released by water cooling to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $Q = 100 \times 1 \times 20 = 2000\text{ cal}$. Heat to melt ALL $20\text{ g}$ ice: $20 \times 80 = 1600\text{ cal}$. Total water mass $= 100 + 20 = 120\text{ g}$. Final temperature $T = \frac{400}{120 \times 1} = 3.33^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: An iron block of mass $2\text{ kg}$ is heated to $400^\circ\text{C}$ and dropped into a large block of ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$. If $s_{\text{iron}} = 470\text{ J/kg K}$ and $L_f = 3.36 \times 10^5\text{ J/kg}$, calculate the mass of ice melted.
explanation: Heat lost by iron block cooling to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $Q = m s \Delta T = 2 \times 470 \times 400 = 376,000\text{ J}$. Mass of ice melted $m_{\text{ice}} = \frac{Q}{L_f} = \frac{376000}{3.36 \times 10^5} \approx 1.119\text{ kg} \approx 1.12\text{ kg}$.

subject: Physics
question: A heater rated $P = 1\text{ kW}$ is used to heat $2\text{ kg}$ of liquid of specific heat $s = 2000\text{ J/kg K}$ from $20^\circ\text{C}$ to $80^\circ\text{C}$. If heat loss to surroundings occurs at a constant rate of $100\text{ W}$, calculate the total time required.
explanation: Heat required $Q = m s \Delta T = 2 \times 2000 \times (80 - 20) = 4000 \times 60 = 240,000\text{ J}$. Effective heating power $P_{\text{eff}} = P - P_{\text{loss}} = 1000 - 100 = 900\text{ W}$. Time $t = \frac{Q}{P_{\text{eff}}} = \frac{240000}{900} = 266.67\text{ seconds} \approx 266.7\text{ s}$.

subject: Physics
question: In a continuous flow calorimeter, water flows through a tube at a rate of $m = 2.0\text{ g/s}$ past a heating coil of power $P = 42\text{ W}$. Find the steady-state temperature rise $\Delta T$ of the water. (Take $s_{\text{water}} = 4.2\text{ J/g K}$)
explanation: Rate of heat supply $P = \left(\frac{dm}{dt}\right) s \Delta T \implies 42 = 2.0 \times 4.2 \times \Delta T = 8.4 \Delta T \implies \Delta T = \frac{42}{8.4} = 5.0^\circ\text{C}$.

subject: Physics
question: Two identical bodies of mass $m$ and specific heat $s$ are at temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$ ($T_1 > T_2$). If a Carnot heat engine operates between them until their temperatures equalize at $T_f$, the maximum work obtained is:
explanation: For reversible Carnot operation, entropy change $\Delta S = m s \ln\left(\frac{T_f}{T_1}\right) + m s \ln\left(\frac{T_f}{T_2}\right) = 0 \implies T_f = \sqrt{T_1 T_2}$. Max work $W = Q_1 - Q_2 = m s (T_1 - T_f) - m s (T_f - T_2) = m s (T_1 + T_2 - 2 T_f) = m s (T_1 + T_2 - 2\sqrt{T_1 T_2})$.

subject: Physics
question: A $50\text{ g}$ piece of ice at $-20^\circ\text{C}$ is added to $50\text{ g}$ of water at $40^\circ\text{C}$ in a calorimeter. Calculate the mass of ice remaining unmelted in the mixture.
explanation: Heat released by water cooling to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $50 \times 1 \times 40 = 2000\text{ cal}$. Heat to warm ice from $-20^\circ\text{C}$ to $0^\circ\text{C}$: $50 \times 0.5 \times 20 = 500\text{ cal}$. Heat remaining to melt ice $= 2000 - 500 = 1500\text{ cal}$. Mass of ice melted $= \frac{1500}{80} = 18.75\text{ g}$. Mass of ice remaining $= 50 - 18.75 = 31.25\text{ g}$.

subject: Physics
question: A bullet of mass $m$ travelling horizontally at speed $v$ strikes a stationary wooden block of mass $M$ suspended by a string and gets embedded. If $90\%$ of lost kinetic energy goes into heating the bullet of specific heat $s$, the rise in bullet temperature is:
explanation: KE loss in inelastic collision $\Delta K = \frac{1}{2} \frac{m M}{m + M} v^2$. Heat absorbed $Q = 0.90 \Delta K = 0.45 \frac{m M}{m + M} v^2$. Temperature rise $m s \Delta T = Q \implies \Delta T = \frac{0.45 M v^2}{(M + m) s}$.
